The test image shows a young soybean seedling that has collapsed/wilted at the soil line, with dead/dried leaves. The stem appears damaged at or near the soil surface. This looks like a seedling disease affecting the stem at the soil line.

Top candidates: **Rhizoctonia** (dry reddish-brown canker at soil line), **Pythium_damping_off** (water-soaked lesions), **Phytophthora** (brown stem rot from soil up), **Fusarium** (root rot with brown vascular tissue).

Looking at the references: Rhizoctonia shows reddish-brown dry cankers at the soil line (matches well), Phytophthora shows wilted/dead plants with brown stem discoloration, Pythium shows water-soaked early seedling rot. Let me check a few more:
I've now viewed 8 reference images. Let me view 4 more to reach the minimum 12 requirement:

## Analysis

**Test image features:**
- Young soybean seedling that has collapsed/died at the soil line
- Dried, brown/tan wilted leaves
- Dark discoloration visible near the stem-soil junction
- Dry, sandy soil conditions
- Plant appears to have been girdled/killed at the hypocotyl

**Ruling out candidates:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Reference shows water-soaked, mushy cotyledons in very wet/dark soil — inconsistent with the dry sandy conditions here
- **Phytophthora**: Typically affects more mature plants in wet/poorly-drained conditions; shows dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward
- **Fusarium**: Shows internal root/vascular browning; root system heavily rotted/blackened
- **Charcoal_Rot**, **SDS**, **White_Mold**: All affect mature plants, not seedlings at this stage
- **Diaporthe**, **Septoria**, **Downy_Mildew**: Leaf/stem diseases of mature plants

**Best match — Rhizoctonia:**
- Causes reddish-brown, sunken, **firm and dry** cankers on the hypocotyl at the soil line
- Matches the dry sandy soil context (Rhizoctonia thrives in warmer, drier conditions)
- The Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-left panel) shows a nearly identical scenario: hand holding a young collapsed seedling with a reddish-brown canker at the soil line
- Wilted/dead seedlings scattered in field with dry canker girdling the stem is the hallmark presentation
